records.source_paraphrase: Some astrologers favor yogas while others maintain that prediction of lifespan requires dasha-period schemes; the source reports both camps.
records.critical_limit: Competing methodological scopes, not evidence one method is accurate; high-stakes mortality not personal advice.

records.source_paraphrase: The source defines short life below 32, medium from 32 to 70, long above 70, and upper-excellent beyond 100 years.
records.critical_limit: Midlife interval at exact age32 conflicts with Chapter XII introduction's 33–70; literal source thresholds retained.

records.source_paraphrase: The translated text says astrologers cannot accurately assess a child's lifespan until age 12.
records.critical_limit: Source self-limitation contradicts blanket infant-death timing claims elsewhere; do not apply medically.

records.source_paraphrase: The author distinguishes three groups of childhood-death claims associated with parent conditions, infancy rulers and alleged short-life yogas.
records.critical_limit: Historically framed nonclinical assertions, not child welfare or medical evidence.

records.source_paraphrase: Jupiter in lagna, strong benefic lord, bright/full Moon and benefic D9 conditions are given as cancellation of unfavorable short-life chart combinations.
records.critical_limit: Explicit reverse/mitigating cases must be frozen before tests; do not posthoc rescue or make death predictions.

records.source_paraphrase: The appearance/rising of Agastya and the Seven Rishis is presented as a cancellation of natal adversity.
records.critical_limit: Extra sky-visibility/astronomy context beyond planets; actual sighting and original time astronomical horizon ambiguous.

records.source_paraphrase: The author says medium lifespan is 33 through 70 years, which is not perfectly aligned with Chapter X's medium starting at 32.
records.critical_limit: No hidden normalization of 32 to 33; potential inclusive-year ambiguity requires Sanskrit check.

records.source_paraphrase: A succession of conditional planetary arrangements are said to predict precise ages including 33, 36, 44, 48, 60 and 70 years.
records.critical_limit: High stakes claims are not established medical or actuarial forecasts; no personal application.

records.source_paraphrase: The author says the number of yogas is innumerable and that the reported selection follows Yavanacharya and sages.
records.critical_limit: Explicit coverage limit; don't claim listed combinations comprise complete predictive system or cherry-pick unlisted clauses.

records.source_paraphrase: The work contrasts the Yavana view that yogas conferring wealth/status imply long life with Varahamihira's separate treatment, observing that poor people also survive to old age.
records.critical_limit: Important source-level negative/counterexample to using general 'strength' for both financial and longevity outcomes; not measured predictive validity.

records.source_paraphrase: Verses purport to assign life spans of two thousand, ten thousand, sixty thousand years or a Brahma/Yuga term to some planetary conditions.
records.critical_limit: Biologically impossible as literal human lifespans; may be mythical/metaphoric but cannot reinterpret without original language textual proof.

records.locator: Chapter XII Translator's Note after v18, PDF263
records.source_paraphrase: Bhasin's planetary-hour explanation says first Hora from sunset then constructs worked example from sunrise; the two clocks have different anchors.
records.critical_limit: Do not silently substitute a local-day reference; note requires further source-defined time convention.

records.locator: Lesson8 Brahma Vidya sexagesimal system, PDF157
records.source_paraphrase: Rath introduces his own attempt to compute cycles of Dharma down to an exact year and says this calculation has not been done in earlier available literature.
records.critical_limit: Not ancient Jaimini Sutra and not scientifically verified historical chronology or personal astrology validation.

records.source_paraphrase: The printed sutra straightforwardly introduces the exposition of Upadesa, while Rath interprets syllable counts and alternative splitting as an otherwise hidden Vishnu invocation.
records.critical_limit: Hidden-invocation explanation is translator's religious hermeneutic, not a literal unambiguous source verse or natal prediction.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath interprets the Jaimini technical sutra as saying all named houses/signs/varnada terms are encoded via the Katapayadi phonemic numeral system.
records.critical_limit: Exact Sanskrit decoding/scope and alternative commentary schools must be compared before making this a universally obligatory parser.

records.source_paraphrase: The modern tutorial interprets Lagna as the body/soul identity or purpose attachment and discusses its relation to cognition.
records.critical_limit: Not an independently specified chart-derived personality equation; do not invent metric for spiritual purpose.

scope: Further reading of Bhasin Chapters X–XII and Rath lessons VII, VIII, XI, XII, previously not substantially indexed by this reader. No person-level prediction or model change.
special_qc: SC Chapter X vs Chapter XII medium longevity starts 32 vs 33
SC Chapter XII distinguishes political power vs longevity and acknowledges poverty/longevity counterexamples
SC Chapter XII fantastic thousands-year values are historically attributed, not plausible ordinary human outcomes
Rath exposition/creative Sanskrit readings cannot be attributed automatically to ancient Jaimini
